scope: Theorem 1.1 (Threshold parallel repetition) of the manuscript “Threshold parallel repetition for finite-dimensional entangled games” (preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 277 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ad2fcb38fca09ed7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal constant κ0 > 0 such that the following holds. Let G be any finite two-player one-round game with Boolean acceptance predicate and entangled value v = ω∗(G) < 1. For every 0 < δ < 1 − v, every integer k ≥ 1, and every finite-dimensional joint strategy for k repetitions, Pr[Wk ≥ ⌈(v + δ)k⌉] ≤ exp − κ0δ5 1 + log d k ! . (1) The same inequality holds for the supremum over those strategies.
